Norms: The original study gathered norms of positive affect (M = 35.0, SD = 6.4) and negative affect (M = 18.1, SD = 5.9) from a non-clinical undergraduate sample. Norms from a large-scale clinical sample have not been reported.
Internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha,: The original study found an average Cronbach's alpha of 0.88 for the positive affect items and 0.87 for the negative affect items and showed that these values for each construct remained relatively consistent when reporting affect across time frames up to a year.
Inter-rater reliability: Not enough research has been conducted on inter-rater reliability to give a comprehensive rating.
Test-retest reliability: The original study found an average coefficient of 0.68 for positive affect and 0.71 for negative affect for an 8-week test-retest period when reporting affect across time frames up to a year.
Test-repeatability: Like inter-rater reliability, limited research is available on test-repeatability.
